summary: Koken Unno specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a doctorate from Nagoya University, where he studied under Hidenori Kitagawa, Yoshifumi Ueda, and others. He served as an assistant at Nagoya University (~1964–1971) and professor at Meijo University (~1991–2007).
Koki Kawagishi worked in Buddhist studies. In 1976, he held positions as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University.
Konrad Klaus specializes in Indology and Tibetology. He studied under Michael Hahn from around 1980 to 1985 and held a post at the University of Bonn around 1999.

Kosei Ishii studied at Waseda University (~1969–1978), working in Buddhist studies and philosophy. His academic posts include assistant positions at Waseda University, associate professor at Komazawa Junior College (~1990–2004), and professorships at Komazawa University (~2004–2016) and Nagoya University (attested 2004).

Kosei Mizutani studied at Bukkyo University and Ryukoku University (~1948–1952) in Buddhist studies. He later served at Bukkyo University as an associate professor (~1960–1967) and as president (~1979–1989).

Kosei Tada studied at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1966) in the field of Buddhist studies. He held a post at Taisho University (~1970–2009) and served as president of the Society for Buddhist Cultural Studies (~2003–2007).
Koshin Suzuki completed doctoral studies at Taisho University in Buddhist studies and Indology. He later served as a researcher at Taisho University, attested from 1995 to 1998.

Koshiro Tamaki studied at the University of Tokyo (~1937–1940), specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held posts at Toyo University (~1950–1965), Tohoku University (~1976–1979), Nihon University (~1979–1986), and the University of Tokyo.

Kosho Kawamura studied at Toyo University (~1948–1952) under Giyu Nishi, Nichijin Sakamoto, Koshiro Tamaki, and others in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held several posts at Toyo University (~1956–1994) and lectured at Minobusan University (~1995–2000).
Kosho Uchiyama studied at Waseda University (~1933–1937) in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He trained under and succeeded traditional teacher Kodo Sawaki (~1941–1965).

Kotatsu Fujita studied at the University of Tokyo and Harvard, supervised by Shoson Miyamoto and Hajime Nakamura. Working in Buddhist studies and Indology, he was a professor at Hokkaido University (~1966–1989) and former president of Sapporo Otani Junior College (~1989–1993).
Koun Kajiyoshi worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held an academic post at Taisho University.
Koun Yamada was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at First Higher School and Tokyo Imperial University. He succeeded Hakuun Yasutani and was employed at NOF Corporation.
Koyo Shimizu studied Buddhist studies under Shoko Takeuchi. He served as a part-time lecturer at Ryukoku University, attested in 1995.
Koyu Tamura studied at the University of Tokyo (~1954–1957) in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held a post at Nishogakusha University and served as a professor at Toyo University (~1980–2002).

Indologist Krishna Kanta Handiqui earned M.A. degrees from the University of Calcutta and the University of Oxford. He served as Principal and Senior Professor at Jagannath Barooah College (~1930–1948) and as Vice-Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1948–1957).

Krishna Mohan Banerjee studied at Hare School and Presidency University, Kolkata, working in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He held posts at Hare School (~1829–1832) and served as Second Professor at Bishop's College, Kolkata (attested 1869–1870).

Krishnanath Chatterjee worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under several teachers, including Surendra Nath Bhattacharya, Haripada Chakravarty, Ramaranjan Mukherji, Krishna Gopal Goswami, Satkari Mookerjee, Amareshwar Thakur, and Siddheshwar Bhattacharya.

Kristin Johnston Largen works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2018, she was attested as Professor of Systematic Theology at United Lutheran Seminary and Associate Dean of Religious and Spiritual Life at Gettysburg College.

Kristin Scheible studied at Colby College and Harvard University, with advisors including Anne E. Monius and Diana L. Eck. Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, she held posts at Harvard, Brown University, and Bard College (attested 2008).
